---
title: "How many standard deviations is a specified value from the sample mean?"
---

## The question

How many standard deviations is a specified value from the sample mean?

## What to check and do

1. Compute the observed mean and sample standard deviation. 2. Subtract the mean from the chosen value. 3. Divide by the standard deviation; stop if it is zero.

## Worked example: iris

This example uses a public dataset distributed with R. It does not make claims about observations outside that dataset.

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("iris")
answer <- ru_apply("z_score", data=d, x="Sepal.Length", threshold=7)
stopifnot(length(answer)==1L,is.finite(answer))
```

A positive z-score places the chosen sepal length above the overall sample mean. Mixing distinct groups can make that overall comparison misleading.

## Apply the method to another question

Replace the data frame and column names with those in your own file:

```r
ru_apply("z_score", data=your_data, x="numeric_column", threshold=7)
```

If you need one z-score for each observed value, omit threshold; if comparing within species, standardize separately within species.


## Inspect conditions

Use `ru_plan("z_score")` for available-versus-missing input routes. A calculation can run even when its assumptions do not justify an inference.
